TIMSS and PISA country trends

TIMSS: grade x subject, 1995-2023 / PISA: sex x subject, 2000-2022

Published

October 22, 2026

1 Introduction

  • This page plots country trends in two international student assessments:
    • TIMSS, 1995-2023, by grade (4, 8) and subject (mathematics, science).
    • PISA, 2000-2022, by sex and subject (mathematics, reading, science).
  • Japan, Korea, the United States and Finland are highlighted against all other participants, with the mean of all economies in light green.
  • Scores are read from saved files (World Bank EdStats, IEA TIMSS 2023, the PISA 2022 student file); nothing is downloaded at render.
  • Sections: Data (sources, exclusions, coverage), TIMSS, PISA (all participants; a fixed set of economies), Reading the figures.

2 Data

  • TIMSS (Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study, IEA) tests grade 4 and grade 8 students in mathematics and science, every 4 years.
  • PISA (Programme for International Student Assessment, OECD) tests 15-year-olds in mathematics, reading and science, every 3 years. It has no grade dimension, so its rows are sex instead.
Source
  • World Bank EdStats API, source 12: LO.TIMSS.MAT4/MAT8/SCI4/SCI8 (1995-2019) and LO.PISA.MAT/REA/SCI with .FE/.MA sex splits (2000-2018).
  • IEA TIMSS 2023 International Results, Exhibits 1.1.1 / 1.2.1 (mathematics, grade 4 / 8) and 2.1.1 / 2.2.1 (science, grade 4 / 8), xlsx from https://timss2023.org/ Download Center.
  • PISA 2022 (not in EdStats; OECD table pages refuse automated download, 403): student-weighted (stu_wgt) means by country and sex from the full OECD PISA 2022 student file as redistributed by the learningtower project (student_2022.rds, https://github.com/kevinwang09/learningtower).
    • Check: the same computation on student_2018.rds reproduces the World Bank 2018 values within 0.5 (all) / 0.7 (by sex) points on average, max 4.1 points (Table 2).
    • These are point estimates only; no standard errors (OECD’s replicate-weight method is not applied).
  • Exclusions
    • World Bank regional and income aggregates.
    • TIMSS 2023 benchmarking entities (e.g. Dubai, Quebec).
    • TIMSS 2023 estimates flagged “not reliably measured” (South Africa grade 4 science, Cote d’Ivoire grade 8).
    • TIMSS 2023 participants with no EdStats series 1995-2019 (England, Belgium Flemish / French, Chinese Taipei).
  • PISA keeps every participant in the data, including the 2022-only entries outside the World Bank economy list: Chinese Taipei (TAP), Baku (QAZ), Ukrainian regions (QUR). Kosovo’s OECD code KSV is mapped to XKX.

3 TIMSS

4 PISA

4.1 All participating economies

  • Lines: every PISA participant in the data, in every cycle it took part in (92 World Bank economies plus Chinese Taipei, Baku and Ukrainian regions in 2022).
  • Mean (light green): unweighted mean over the economies tested in that year, so its composition changes across cycles.

4.2 PISA with a fixed set of economies

  • Lines: all 42 economies tested in PISA 2000, in every cycle each took part in.
  • Mean (light green): to remove compositional change, each panel’s mean uses only the PISA 2000 economies with a score in every cycle 2000-2022: 31 in the mathematics and science panels, 29 in the reading panels.
    • Drawn but outside the mean (a cycle missing): Albania, Argentina, Bulgaria, Chile, Israel, North Macedonia, Peru, Romania (no 2003), Liechtenstein (no 2015-2022), Russian Federation (no 2022), Luxembourg (absent from the 2022 student file used here).
    • Reading panels only: United States (no reading 2006), Spain (no reading 2018).
  • The y-axis starts at 450 (zoom only): economies scoring below 450 are out of view but still enter the mean.

5 Reading the figures

  • Each grey line is one economy; points are test years.
  • Highlighted: Japan (red, bold), Korea (blue), United States (purple), Finland (orange).
  • The light-green line is the unweighted mean over the economies tested in that year. The set of economies changes across cycles, so a move in the mean can reflect entry or exit of countries, not only score changes (e.g. the grade 8 dip in 2007-2011 in Figure 1; not tested here).
  • Scores are on each study’s own scale (centre 500, std 100 at its base year); TIMSS and PISA scores are not comparable with each other.
